key_insight: TRACE models day-by-day multimodal hospital trajectories and reports the highest AUROC across nine inpatient risk-prediction settings.
clinical_relevance: The framework could support assessment of in-hospital mortality, prolonged length of stay, and readmission risk, but clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Separates day-invariant context from daily EHR, chest x-ray, radiology-report, and discharge-summary events.
Uses temporal attention to encode trajectories, with unavailable modalities emitting no tokens.
Applies phenotype-guided contrastive learning and attributes predictions to hospital days and modalities.
evidence_signal: Across nearly 180,000 stays from MIMIC-IV, eICU, and MIMIC-III, TRACE achieved the highest AUROC in all nine dataset-task settings and highest accuracy in eight.
watch_item: Because discharge summaries are included, task-specific time cutoffs require careful verification to prevent use of information unavailable at prediction time.
paper_title: TRACE: Tracking Multimodal Clinical Trajectories for Inpatient Risk Prediction
